report.total_time: About 1 hr 57 min, from peeling garlic to the asparagus coming out from under the broiler, plus about 2 more minutes to slice the steak and plate. The screen promised "about 1 hr 55 min", so that was close. My clock: potatoes went in at about 0:46. Applesauce was mashed by about 1:15. Potatoes came out at about 1:46 and the asparagus was done at about 1:55. Prep ran a little long, because peeling 8 cloves, muddling the paste and hasselback-slicing 8 potatoes took me about 45 min before the first timer. The later steps then had small gaps that soaked up the difference.

Up next: Hasselback Potatoes', and no step tells you to take the asparagus out. Step 32 doesn't even list its timer any more. Done literally, the asparagus stays in the oven through the potato step and is still inside when step 33 switches the oven to broil, so it overcooks before the parmesan goes on.

literal_failures.step: 19 (applesauce: 'Microwave 7-8 minutes on high. Stir it all around again.')
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: The stir happens after the timer, but by then the screen has moved on to steps 20 and 21. When the timer rings you're looking at step 21, 'Microwave another 7-8 minutes', which doesn't mention stirring. Following the current screen, you skip the stir and get uneven cooking.

literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: No amounts are given, and the screen just had you make a whole batch of garlic paste (8 cloves, about 3 tbsp). Done literally, you stir in all of it, but the card wants 1 tsp. That's about 9 times too much garlic, plus the paste's 1/2 tsp of salt on top of the salt you add.

literal_failures.step: 13 (applesauce prep: 'Juice the half lemon')
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: Step 11 has just used a whole lemon for the asparagus (half juiced, half sliced into rings), so 'the half lemon' doesn't exist. You either take the asparagus juice or need a second lemon the screen never mentions.

ten_minutes_late.when: Steps 29-30, the steak sear and baste. A realistic cause is having to go and find the thermometer, which the screen never asked for in advance, or a thicker steak needing longer.
ten_minutes_late.what_happens: The asparagus timer (started at step 28) and the potato timer (started at step 25) keep running. The asparagus rings while you're stuck at the pan, so you either leave the steak or let the asparagus roast up to 10 min too long and go limp. The potatoes ring and sit in the oven 5-10 min past the plan; they're forgiving, but the garlic coating starts to darken. The broiler step is pushed back, so the potatoes and steak wait even longer. The pinned live timers do show what's really running and how long is left, which helps. But the static 'Timers running as you start this' and 'Nothing needs you for about N min' lines under each step are now wrong. The screen has no 'you're behind' signal and no clock, so you have to work out from the live timers that the asparagus needs pulling now. Nothing on the current step tells you.

food_risks.risk: No step tells you to pull it when the timer rings, so it can overcook or be left in while the broiler heats. If it is pulled, it sits about 6-9 min before broiling. And no step says to take it out from under the broiler, where parmesan burns in under a minute.

The rest starts at about 1:42 and serving is around 1:57, so it rests about 15 min against the card's 5-10, and comes to the table lukewarm. Seasoning 'right before it goes in' is interrupted by loading the asparagus while the oil smokes.

Step 32 takes them out and says 'serve hot' about 8-10 min before the meal is ready, so they cool and lose their crisp edges. If they need the full 20 min, they clash with switching the oven to broil.
It's done about 40 min early. Harmless, since the card says it's good warm or cold, but it isn't warm if that was intended.

report.headings:
The screen had no phase headings, only the [Recipe, card step N] tag on each step. The tags helped me know which card to check. Landmarks would have helped in three places:
- Before step 16: "Prep done; potatoes go in; first timer starts". The 15 prep steps blur together.
- Before step 25: "Final stretch, about 30 min to the table: steak and asparagus". This is where the hands-on load jumps.
- At the end: a "Serve" step that gathers slicing the steak, pulling the asparagus and plating.
top_problems: The ends of dishes are missing or misplaced. The asparagus 'Pull the pan out' is buried in the step where it goes in, and no step follows its timer ringing. The last step never takes the asparagus out from under the broiler. There is no slice-steak or serve-everything step, and the potatoes are told to 'serve hot' about 8 min before anything else is ready.

No quantities or equipment on the screen. Every measuring step sends you to a card (about 10 lookups). Literally, 'garlic paste' in step 9 means the whole 3 tbsp batch instead of 1 tsp. The thermometer and the second lemon are never flagged.

Actions that follow a timer are attached to the step that starts the timer. The applesauce stir after the first 7-8 min and the asparagus pull both get lost because the screen has moved on when the timer rings. Also, the printed 'min left' figures under steps 20-22 contradict each other.
worked_well: The 'Timers running as you start this' lists and the 'Nothing needs you for about N min. Up next: X' cues made the long middle stretch (applesauce, steak sit-out, potatoes baking) calm and easy to follow.
Done-when cues and 'stay with it' flags at the critical moments (oil just smoking, 130F inside, undisturbed sear, broiling parmesan) told me exactly when to stand at the stove.

The overall order is sensible. Potatoes go in first and get their mid-bake baste, the steak comes out of the fridge at a reasonable time, and the asparagus shares the 200C oven with the potatoes before the oven switches to broil after the potatoes are out.
data_issues: The garlic paste recipe makes about 3 tbsp from 8 cloves, but the potatoes use 1 tsp. The plan makes the full batch, which takes about 12 min of extra work. The card itself notes that a microplane into the butter would be faster for a small amount.
Yields don't match. Ribeye serves 1 (one 12 oz steak), potatoes serve 4 (8 potatoes), asparagus serves 8 (2 lb), and the applesauce makes 3 cups.
The meal needs 1.5 lemons: 1 for the asparagus, half for the applesauce. Both prep steps assume one lemon.
The asparagus card says 'for 8 to 10 minutes' but also 'thick spears nearer 12'. The timer is 8-12.
The applesauce card's notes say to uncover away from your face, but no step says to cover the dish.
The ribeye card's 'Before you start' (thermometer) and its ingredients (herbs, butter) have no prep step in the plan. Ribeye prep only peels garlic.
Hasselback card 'Prep: 15 min' is optimistic. Scrubbing and hasselback-slicing 8 potatoes takes more like 15-20 min on its own.
The plan puts asparagus loading (step 28) between seasoning the steak and laying it in the pan, while the oil is already smoking. It should come before the pan goes on.
The plan's timer bookkeeping is internally inconsistent (potatoes 30 to 20 vs steak 30 to 25 over the same gap), which suggests the step-duration estimates behind it are off.
Asparagus prep (step 11) has you juice the lemon, and step 24 repeats the squeeze. The data duplicates the action across the prep and card steps.

ten_minutes_late.when: Around steps 25-26: the potato baste takes longer (the reserved butter has set and needs re-warming, the tray is awkward), or the pan is slow to reach smoking point, so the steak goes in about 10 min later than planned.
ten_minutes_late.what_happens: The potato second-bake timer started at step 25 keeps running. It rings while the steak is searing or being basted (steps 29-30), but the sequence still puts potato removal at step 32, after the steak rest. You either leave the steak mid-baste to pull a tray or leave the potatoes in about 10 min too long (dark, possibly burnt edges, garlic scorching). The asparagus, which goes in at step 28 after the pan heats, ends 10 min later too. It finishes during or after the steak rest, then needs the broiler heat-up and broil, so the steak rests 15+ min and the potatoes sit out longer. The pinned live timers help: you can see the potatoes at 0 while you're on a steak step. But the step list doesn't re-plan, the 'timers running as you start this' lines and the 'Nothing needs you for X min' notes go stale and wrong, and there's no clock or phase marker showing how far behind you are. So the screen shows you're behind, but not what to do about it. Being late earlier (prep before step 16, or the applesauce) is harmless, because the timers only start on tap.

The rest runs past 10 min: rest starts at step 31, then potatoes, broiler heat-up and the parmesan broil all have to happen before anyone eats, and slicing is never scheduled. It's served lukewarm.
Pulled at step 32 and told to 'serve hot', then they sit about 6-7 min while the asparagus finishes. Hasselbacks hold heat, so the risk is moderate.
The oil can overheat while you load the asparagus into the oven between heating the pan and laying in the steak, giving acrid smoke and a bitter crust.
The missed stir makes it uneven. It's done about 40 min before serving, but the card says it's good warm or cold, so the timing itself is fine.

report.headings: My screen had no phase headings. Landmarks would have helped in three places: (1) a 'Before you start / prep' block (steps 1-16), which takes about 45 min with no timers running, and where a heading could carry a gather list with the thermometer, 1.5 lemons, two oven racks and the quantities; (2) 'While the potatoes bake' (steps 17-24), to show these are flexible and safe to fall behind on; (3) 'Final stretch: about 20 min, stay in the kitchen' before step 25, where oven, stove and timers all converge and a mistake costs food. A closing 'Plate up' landmark is also missing; the screen just stops after the parmesan broil.
top_problems: When an action comes after a step's timer, it gets lost because the screen moves on as soon as the timer starts. The applesauce stir (step 19) is skipped, and the asparagus's 'Pull the pan out' (step 28) is never repeated. The asparagus timer rings during a step that says 'Nothing needs you', so the asparagus overcooks.

The ending is broken. The potatoes are told to 'serve hot' (step 32) about 6-7 min before the asparagus is done, the steak is never sliced or served, its rest overruns, and there's no final plate-up step, so the cook has to put the meal together alone during the busiest moment.

Steps carry no quantities and leave out prerequisites from the cards: about 15 card lookups, no thermometer warning, a lemon count that doesn't add up ('the half lemon' after the whole lemon is used), no mention of a second oven rack. The static 'timers running' lines also disagree with each other (the steak-to-potato gap jumps between 0, 5, 2 and 3 min).
worked_well: The running-timer list and the 'Nothing needs you for about X min. Up next: ...' notes made the waits clear. I always knew the next thing coming and roughly how long I had.

The interleaving is sensible overall. The garlic paste comes first because the potato mixture needs it, the oven is switched on in time for the potatoes, and the applesauce and asparagus prep fit into the 40-min bake. The steak's 30-min sit-out ends right as the potatoes get basted, and the asparagus shares the 200C oven with no temperature change until the broil.
Done-when cues and 'stay with it' flags on the critical steps (smoking oil, 130F, undisturbed sear, watching the broil) show where attention matters.
data_issues: Garlic Paste makes about 3 tbsp from 8 cloves, but the potatoes use only 1 tsp. The plan doesn't scale it down or say what to do with the rest, and the card's note about subtracting the paste's salt isn't carried into the potato seasoning.
Mismatched servings: the ribeye serves 1, the potatoes serve 4 (8 potatoes), the asparagus serves 8 (2 lb). Nothing in the plan scales them to a common number of diners.
The asparagus card gives '8 to 10 minutes' in the text, 'thick nearer 12' in the same sentence, and a timer of 8-12 min.
The applesauce card never says whether to cover the dish, but its notes say 'Uncover away from your face'.
The ribeye has no time for step 5 (flip and baste to 130F); only the overall 'Cook: 8 min' hints at it.
The plan schedules the asparagus into the oven (step 28) after heating the steak pan (step 26) instead of before, so smoking oil sits unattended.

The plan orders the asparagus finish (broiler heat-up plus broil, about 6 min) after the steak rest and potato removal, so the steak's rest overruns. Starting the asparagus a few minutes earlier, or holding the potatoes in the oven, would line things up.
Parsley chopping and steak slicing have no slot in the plan. The parsley falls into the final crunch and the slicing never appears.
The lemon requirement across recipes adds up to 1.5 lemons, but nothing in the plan totals shared ingredients.

report.total_time: About 1 hr 55 min to 2 hr 05 min in my dry run, so roughly what the screen promised (about 1 hr 55 min). Prep (steps 1-16) took me about 45-52 min: garlic paste about 10-12, scrubbing 8 potatoes about 3, asparagus prep about 8-10, and slicing 8 hasselbacks about 12-16. From the potatoes going in to the last broil was about 64-66 min: potatoes go in at T=0 and ring at T=40, I baste and return them at about T=42, the steak goes in at about T=48, the steak rests at about T=56, potatoes come out at about T=58-60, then 3 min of broiler heat-up plus 2-3 min of broil ends at about T=65. Wherever you fall behind, it adds straight to the total, because every timer only starts when you tap Next.

literal_failures.step: 19 (applesauce: Microwave 7-8 min. Stir it all around again.)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: The stir has to happen after the 7-8 min timer, but the timer only starts when you tap Next, and that moves you on to step 20 (steak out). When the timer rings, step 21 just says 'Microwave another 7-8 minutes', with no stir. A literal cook never stirs between the two rounds, so the apples cook unevenly and the top pieces dry out.

literal_failures.step: 28 (asparagus: Roast 8-12 min... Pull the pan out.)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: 'Pull the pan out' belongs to the end of the timer, but you tap Next straight onto the steak sear. The timer rings during step 30 (basting) or step 31. Step 31 says 'Nothing needs you for about 4 min. Up next: Hasselback Potatoes', and nothing on screen tells you to take the asparagus out. A literal cook leaves it in until step 33, then switches the oven to broil with the asparagus still inside. It overcooks, and step 34's 'scatter the parmesan and broil' assumes the pan is out on the counter.

literal_failures.step: 30 (steak: pull at 130F inside)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: You need an instant-read thermometer, but the screen never says to have one ready. The card's 'Before you start' line was dropped. If you find out at this point, you are mid-baste with no way to check doneness.

literal_failures.step: 32 (potatoes: take out, chop parsley, serve hot)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: Parsley was never prepped, so you chop it now while the potatoes cool. 'Serve hot' comes before the asparagus has even had its broil: about 3 min of broiler heat-up plus 2-3 min of broiling are still to come, and the steak is still resting. Doing exactly what it says means serving potatoes alone, about 6 min before the rest of the meal.

literal_failures.step: 34 (last step)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: The screen ends at 'broil 2 to 3 minutes'. There is no step to take the asparagus out, slice the steak, plate everything or bring out the applesauce. Steak slicing is only implied in step 31.

literal_failures.step: 8 (garlic paste: use immediately, or stir in oil, jar and refrigerate)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: You make about 3 tbsp of paste but the potatoes need 1 tsp. The screen offers 'use immediately OR jar', when the real answer is to do both: use 1 tsp and jar the rest. Taken literally, you could put all the paste into the potato butter.

literal_failures.step: 26 to 29 (heat oil until smoking, then pat and season the steak, then put the asparagus in the oven, then lay the steak in)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: Following the order, the oil reaches the smoking point and then you leave it for 1-2 min while you pat and season the steak and walk the asparagus tray into the oven. The pan overheats and the kitchen fills with smoke. The asparagus should go in before the pan is heated.

literal_failures.step: 13 (applesauce: Juice the half lemon.)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: Step 11 has already used the whole asparagus lemon (half juiced, half sliced into rings), so there is no 'half lemon' left. You need a second lemon, and the screen never says so.

ten_minutes_late.when: Phase 5, steps 25-30. For example, the set butter fights you at step 25 and the pan is slow to smoke at step 26, so you start the steak about 10 min later than planned.
ten_minutes_late.what_happens: The potato timer (started at step 25) keeps running, so the potatoes ring while the steak is in its undisturbed sear or while you are basting it. On screen the potato step (32) is still four steps away, so a literal cook leaves them in about 10 min too long and they come out over-browned and dry. Because the asparagus only goes in at step 28, it shifts too, and its ring lands in the middle of basting. The broil at the end gets pushed back, so the potatoes, already out, sit 10-15 min and go lukewarm. The pinned live timers show the potato time running out. But the screen shows no clock times, and its printed 'about N min left' estimates are already inconsistent (steps 20-22), so comparing them with the live timers doesn't show you how far behind you are. The Phase 5 heading only tells you that you are in the final stretch. Being late during prep, by contrast, costs nothing, because no timer is running yet.

food_risks.risk: High risk of overcooking: the 'pull the pan out' instruction is lost, and its ring comes during the steak baste. It is also served last, about 6 min after the potatoes. Roasted at T≈47-57, then pulled, then broiled at about T≈63.
'Serve hot' at step 32, then they wait about 6 min for the broiler heat-up and broil. If you're behind, they overbake because their finish step is queued behind the steak.

Resting starts at about T=56 and the meal is ready at about T=65. That is within the 5-10 min rest, but the steak cools if the asparagus runs long. If you don't notice the missing thermometer, the doneness is a guess.

Done about 35-40 min before serving, so it is room temperature by dinner. The card says that's fine warm or cold, but if you wanted it warm it isn't. It is also unevenly cooked if the stir between rounds is missed.

report.headings: The headings helped somewhat. 'Phase 1: Prep' clearly bounds the mise en place, and 'Phase 3: Hasselback Potatoes in the oven (40 min)' is a good anchor, because the potato timer drives everything after it. Three headings were weak or misleading. 'Phase 2: Start cooking' covers only slicing the potatoes and putting them on the tray, so no cooking happens in it. 'Phase 4: Pan-Seared Ribeye sitting out (30 min)' is named after a timer that needs nothing from you, while the actual work in it is applesauce and asparagus. 'Phase 5: Hasselback Potatoes in the oven (18 min) — then serve' puts the steak sear, the busiest part of the meal, under a potato label, and its 'then serve' clashes with the broil tail after the potatoes come out. A separate landmark such as 'Steak in the pan' or 'Final broil' would have helped more at the crunch.
top_problems: Instructions that belong to the end of a timer ('Pull the pan out' in step 28, 'Stir it all around again' in step 19) sit on the step that starts the timer and disappear when you tap Next. The asparagus is left in the oven during the steak baste and is still in when you switch to broil.

The final stretch is overloaded and poorly shown. The continuous steak baste (no thermometer reminder) overlaps the asparagus and potato rings. The pan sits smoking while you load the asparagus. Potatoes are 'served hot' at step 32 about 6 min before the asparagus is ready, and there is no final serve or plating step.

Too many quantities and too much ingredient logic live only on the cards (about 12 lookups). That includes lemon confusion ('the half lemon' when a second lemon is needed) and a 3-tbsp garlic paste for a 1-tsp use. The printed 'timers running' estimates also disagree with each other.
worked_well: Timers start on Next, and all the hands-on prep comes before the first timer, so a slow cook can't wreck anything during prep.
The 'Nothing needs you for about N min. Up next: X' lines, together with the timers pinned at the top, make the waits in Phases 3-4 calm and clear.
The steak sit-out is started alongside the potatoes' first bake, and the asparagus is fitted into the potato oven so the oven is never preheated twice. The overall order is sensible.
data_issues: The garlic paste recipe makes about 3 tbsp from 8 cloves (about 10-12 min of work), but the potatoes use 1 tsp. The plan doesn't scale it down or say to jar the rest, and the card's own note says a microplane would be faster.
The servings don't match: the steak serves 1, the potatoes serve 4 (8 potatoes), the asparagus serves 8 (2 lb) and the applesauce makes about 3 cups.
Lemons: the asparagus needs 1 whole lemon and the applesauce needs half another, but the data words the applesauce prep as 'Juice the half lemon'.
The asparagus card contradicts itself: 'Roast 8 to 10 minutes' versus 'thick spears nearer 12' and the 8-12 min timer.
The ribeye's thermometer requirement ('Before you start') isn't carried into the step data.
The salt already in the garlic paste isn't subtracted from the potato seasoning, so the potatoes may be over-salted.
The order puts heating the steak pan (step 26) and seasoning it (step 27) before the asparagus goes in the oven (step 28), so the oil smokes unattended. The asparagus should go in first.
The plan has no closing serve step for the steak, asparagus or applesauce. The potato 'serve hot' step comes before the asparagus broil, and the broil can't start until the potatoes leave the oven.
Steps whose action happens when a timer ends ('Stir it all around again', 'Pull the pan out') aren't split into their own after-timer step.
The steak's 30-min sit-out actually becomes about 37 min before it goes in the pan. That's harmless, but the timer rings with nothing to do.
The 'timers running' estimates in steps 20-22 don't agree with each other: the potato and steak timers lose different amounts of time between the same steps.

ten_minutes_late.when: Step 26 onward: the pan is slow to smoke, or I fumble the seasoning and asparagus, and fall 10 min behind while the potatoes' 15–20 min timer is running.
ten_minutes_late.what_happens: The potato timer rings in the middle of steps 29–30, while I'm searing and basting the steak with 'stay with it'. The screen's next potato step (32) comes only after the steak rest, so following the order leaves the potatoes in about 10 extra minutes. They over-brown, and the garlic butter may scorch. The asparagus goes in 10 min late too, so it finishes during the rest or after it, and the broil pushes serving later still: the steak rests about 15–20 min and goes lukewarm. The pinned timers do show that the potato timer has run out, which is the only cue I have. But all of this happens inside Phase 5, so the heading doesn't help me see where I am, and no step tells me what to drop or reorder. If instead I fall behind earlier (say apple prep in step 17 takes 20 min), the slack around the applesauce and the steak's sitting time absorbs most of it, and the potatoes just bake a few minutes past 40 before basting. Not a disaster.

It goes into the pan about 33 min before the asparagus is done. The rest stretches past 10 min (about 11 in my run, more if anything slips), so it's lukewarm at the table. The smoking pan is also left waiting through steps 27–28.
They come out and get 'served hot' at step 32, then sit about 6–8 min while the asparagus broils. They lose crispness and heat.

report.headings: Mixed. Phase 1 (Prep) and Phase 3 ('Hasselback Potatoes in the oven (40 min)') were useful landmarks: they told me the long passive stretch had started. Phase 2 'Start cooking' was misleading, since it's only slicing. Phase 4 'Ribeye sitting out (30 min)' marks a timer, but most of the work under it is applesauce and asparagus, so the heading names the least important thing. Phase 5 is where headings should help most and do least. It's labelled for the potatoes, gives '18 min', which matches no timer, and says '— then serve'. But it holds the whole crunch: heat the pan, sear, baste, roast and pull the asparagus, rest, potatoes out, preheat the broiler, broil. A separate heading for 'Final sear and finish (everything at once)', or one at the broil, would have warned me to clear the decks. When I was running late they didn't help me find my place, because everything late happens under one heading.
top_problems: The finishing stretch (steps 26–34) piles the steak sear, the asparagus roast with its pull-out, the potatoes coming out, and the broil into about 15 min. The asparagus 'pull the pan out' instruction lives on step 28, so nothing tells you to act when its timer rings during the rest. Step 32 also says 'serve hot' with about 6 min of asparagus still to go.

Timer/Next mechanics break on split steps: the step 19 stir falls after its own timer, and the step 20 wait note conflicts with having to tap Next to start the steak timer. The screen's own timer readouts at steps 21–22 don't agree with each other.

The screen leaves out essentials the cook has to dig for on the cards: quantities on most prep steps, the thermometer, herbs and parsley prep, the second lemon. It also has no final step to slice the steak and plate everything.
worked_well: The long early wait is used well: applesauce, steak tempering and asparagus prep all fit inside the potatoes' first 40 min bake, and the steak timer ends almost exactly when the pan goes on.
Pinned 'timers running' lines and 'Nothing needs you for about N min. Up next: X' make passive stretches clear, and helped me spot a timer that had run out when I was behind.
Grouping all the knife work (garlic, asparagus, lemons) into Phase 1 before the oven is hot keeps the later phases mostly hands-free until the final sear.
data_issues: Garlic paste overproduction: 8 cloves (about 3 tbsp, about 15 min of work) to supply 1 tsp to the potatoes. The card's own note says a microplane would be faster for a quantity this small. Its salt also isn't subtracted from the potatoes' 'salt and pepper'.
Lemon count: the asparagus uses a whole lemon (half juiced, half rings) and the applesauce needs another half. Step 13's 'the half lemon' hides that you need 1.5 lemons.
Asparagus card: step text says 8–10 min, timer says 8–12. Card step 1 (heat oven) is silently merged into the potato preheat, which is fine since both are at 200°C.
The applesauce card never says to cover the dish, but its notes say to 'uncover away from your face'.
Yields don't match: ribeye serves 1, potatoes serve 4 (8 potatoes), asparagus serves 8 (2 lb), applesauce makes 3 cups.
The thermometer requirement is only in the ribeye card's 'Before you start', which the plan drops. Steak thickness (needed to pick 3–4 vs 5 min) isn't given anywhere.

The plan mixes the potato butter mixture at step 9, about 70 min before the second half is used, so it will likely have set. Card order (mixing right before brushing) would have avoided this for the first half.

No ending step: nothing covers slicing the steak, taking the asparagus out after the broil, or bringing all four dishes to the table together. Potato step 8 'serve hot' is used as the serving moment, but it isn't the last step.

Order of steps 26–28: an oven task is placed between seasoning the steak and laying it in the smoking pan, and the asparagus goes in only about 10 min before the potatoes finish, so the broil has to come after everything else.

reports.presentation_is: every step of every recipe in one order, one step at a time, with each step's done-when cue and the timers already running

report.total_time: Day before: about 4 hr 15–20 min in my dry run (30 min for the whites to warm up, about 3 min of prep, about 12 min to whip, fold and shape, 90 min baking, 2 hr cooling, 2 min to put the shell away). The screen says about 4 hr 25 min, so that matches. On the day: about 2 hr 10–15 min. Zesting and juicing 6 lemons took about 12 min. The ice bath timer started about 36 min in, the curd went into the fridge about 66 min in and was ready about 126 min in, and I assembled at about 130 min. The screen says about 2 hr 10 min, which matches if the lemon prep takes 12 min or less. The total does not update when you run late. The Pavlova card says "Total: 4 hr" for the shell. That leaves out the 30 min the whites spend warming up, which the screen includes.

literal_failures.step: On the day, steps 5 to 6 (Blueberry Syrup card step 2, then Lemon Curd card step 3)
literal_failures.what_goes_wrong: Step 5 ends when the sugar has dissolved, but no step says to take the syrup off the heat. Then 7 curd steps come next (simmer, temper, 6 min of cooking, butter, strain, ice bath). Taken literally, the syrup keeps simmering on medium for about another 15–20 min until step 13 strains it. It reduces toward jam and may catch on the bottom of the pan. On the card, steps 2 and 3 come straight after each other, so 'off the heat' is implied. Splitting them up loses that.

ten_minutes_late.when: On the day, steps 8–12: tempering and cooking the curd, with the syrup still simmering on the next burner (for example, the juice takes longer to simmer or the curd takes 16 min to reach 170°F instead of 6)

report.headings: The screen has only two section headings: 'made ahead (the day before)' and 'on the day'. They helped: the yolks and the 2-day keeping time made sense, and the long waits stood out. The bracketed tags on each step ([Lemon Curd, card step 4]) were the most useful landmark, because they made every card lookup instant. Within the day there are no phase headings, and a landmark would have helped in two places. Before step 6, something like 'Curd at the stove, about 15 min hands-on: take the syrup off the heat first, have the thermometer, strainer and plastic wrap ready'. And at step 16, '40 min free: prepare the fruit, wash up, chill the cream bowl'. Without them, the stretch of 7 curd steps in the middle hides the fact that the syrup is still on the burner.
top_problems: Splitting up the steps breaks the syrup. Blueberry Syrup step 2 (simmer) and step 3 (strain) are separated by 7 curd steps, and no step says to take the syrup off the heat. Taken literally, it simmers about 15–20 extra minutes and turns jammy or scorches, while the curd needs both hands.

The screen gives no ingredient amounts, and the card's 'Before you start' items (thermometer, plastic wrap, strainer over a bowl, jar) are missing. About 11 card lookups, several of them during hands-on moments (curd step 7, step 9).

The finish is underspecified. Fruit is never prepared. The whipped cream sits out unrefrigerated for about 13–15 min, after a needless 3 min pause at soft peaks. And step 20 doesn't say how to plate the shell or in what order and amounts to add the toppings. Also, the curd and syrup keep for days but are made on the day, which takes up 2 hr 10 min.
worked_well: The 'Timers running as you start this' lines and the 'Nothing needs you for about X. Up next: Y' lines made the waits and parallel timers easy to follow. You always know what is in progress and what comes next.
Each step is tagged with its recipe and card step number, so every lookup took seconds. The yolks are linked clearly across the two days (save them, they keep 2 days, use them in the curd).

Splitting into 'day before' and 'on the day' with separate totals is clear. Within the curd, the order is clean: the ice bath is set up during the zest rest, the juice heats while you whisk the eggs, and the ice bath leads into the fridge. The 30 min whites rest is made explicit, though the card leaves it out.
data_issues: The Blueberry Syrup recipe has no explicit 'take off the heat' step. Strain directly follows simmer, so that only works when the steps are consecutive. The plan inserts 7 curd steps between them.

The plan makes the lemon curd (keeps 5 days) and the syrup (keeps for days) on the day, which takes 2 hr 10 min. Both could be made the day before, during the pavlova's 3.5 hr in the oven. The curd card itself says it uses the 4 leftover yolks. Only the pavlova was offered as make-ahead.

The plan schedules the whipped cream about 13 min before the curd is ready, so the cream waits unrefrigerated. Whipping it last, after the curd's fridge timer, would be better. Step 17 also starts the cream about 6 min before the syrup is ready, then pauses it for about 3 min.
The plan has no step for the fruit, even though the Pavlova card lists fresh berries as a topping.
The same fine-mesh strainer is scheduled for the curd (step 11) and the syrup (step 13) about 2 min apart, with no time for washing.
The plan's timer math is off: step 14 says the ice bath has 25 min left, then a 10 min wait, then step 15 says 17 min left.
The plan puts 'Heat the oven' after the 30 min whites rest and only about 12 min before the bake, and nothing waits for the oven to reach temperature.
The Pavlova card's Total: 4 hr leaves out the 30 min for the whites to warm up. The screen says 4 hr 25 min.

The recipe folds the cream of tartar in at the end and adds the sugar in two big additions. Both are unusual (cream of tartar usually goes in at the start to stabilise the whites; sugar goes in gradually). Noted only as a recipe-data oddity.
The butter is set out to soften only about 30 min before it's needed. One hour of syrup chilling in a jar may not be 'cold', even though the cream card insists on chilled syrup.

report.total_time: Day before: about 4 hr 30 min (30 min whites rest, ~5 min lining/pulsing, ~5 min waiting at step 3 for the oven to reach 350°F, ~12 min whipping and shaping, 90 min bake, 2 hr cooling in the oven, a minute to box it). The screen said about 4 hr 25 min, so it was close. The extra time came from the oven only being switched on after the 30-minute wait. The syrup's cooling chain (10 min plus 1 hr) has about 20 minutes of slack against the curd's 90-minute chill, so the cream step still works. The pinned timers show how long each running timer has left, which helps a bit. ten_minutes_late.when: On the day, steps 5–9: syrup on one burner, curd juice heating, then tempering and 6 min of whisking. For example, zesting 6 lemons took 20 min instead of 10, or you hunt for the thermometer at step 9.
ten_minutes_late.what_happens: Everything on the curd's path (ice bath, then 1 hr fridge) moves 10 min later, so serving is 10 min later too. The serious damage is to the syrup. It has no timer and, as written, is still on the heat, so it simmers about 25–30 min instead of a few: it over-reduces, may scorch, and leaves too little thick syrup for the cream. Being late at step 13 (strain the syrup) does further harm. The syrup goes into the fridge 10 min later, but step 17 is triggered by the curd's fridge timer, so the cream gets syrup that has only chilled about 45 min. The headings show where you are ('Phase 2: Start cooking'), and the pinned timers show the zest timer has ended. Nothing on screen shows the syrup pan, though, because it has no timer, and with no clock times you can't tell how late you are against serving. The headings mark long waits, not the busy stretch where you fell behind.

food_risks.risk: As written it stays at a simmer from step 5 until step 13, about 15–20 min with nobody watching. It over-reduces or scorches, and you get less syrup that is thicker and possibly bitter.

It's whipped about 15–20 min before the curd is cold and assembly can start, and left at room temperature. It's also made with syrup that hasn't finished its 1-hr chill after only 10 min of cooling. The card warns that warm syrup deflates the cream, so it may be soft or loose.

If you tap through steps 2–3 during the wait, step 4 has you whip whites before they reach room temperature, so they whip to less volume. If you wait first, the oven may not be at 350°F when the meringue is spread.
With no equipment set out, finding the thermometer during step 9's constant whisking risks overshooting 170°F. If the syrup boils over next to it, you're pulled away from the curd.
A small risk: the ice bath is made at step 3 and used about 25 min later at step 12. Some ice will have melted, so it chills less well.

report.headings: They helped a little, mostly on the day before, where they map neatly onto the real stages: prep, whipping, 90 min in the oven, 2 hr cooling. Each tells you at a glance what is happening and for how long. On the day they helped less. The busiest and riskiest stretch (steps 4–11: syrup and curd on two burners) sits under one heading, 'Phase 2: Start cooking', with no landmark inside it. Headings then appear for each wait ('Lemon Curd in the ice bath', 'Blueberry Syrup in the fridge', 'Lemon Curd in the fridge'), where little is happening. The waits overlap, but the phases read as one after another: 'Phase 4: Blueberry Syrup in the fridge (1 hr)' gives way to Phase 5 after one step and 16 min, though the syrup still has 45 min to go. That muddles 'where am I'. They didn't get in the way, but a landmark like 'Two pans at once: syrup + curd' or 'Off the heat' would have mattered more than the wait headings.
top_problems: On the day, the blueberry syrup is never taken off the heat after step 5. As written it keeps simmering through the whole curd cook (about 15–20 min) and over-reduces or scorches. It has no timer, so the pinned list doesn't show it either.

The screen gives no quantities and no equipment set-up. Almost every ingredient step needs a card lookup, and the thermometer, strainer, plastic wrap, jar and topping fruit are never mentioned until the moment you need them.

The order and timing at the end are off. The whipped cream is made about 15 min before the curd is ready and left at room temperature. It uses syrup whose fridge timer hasn't finished, against the card's own warning. Steps 16→17 and 17 ('nothing needs you' while whipping) leave you guessing when to start and when to move on.
worked_well: The running timers listed under each step, with 'Up next', made the overlapping chill times on the day easy to track. I always knew which timer to wait for before the next step (except step 16→17).

Splitting the work into the day before and the day itself, and linking the recipes (save the 4 yolks for the curd, refrigerate them, they keep 2 days), made the make-ahead clear and spread the effort well.

The 'done when' cues (glossy stiff peaks, 170°F, soft vs medium-firm peaks) and the practical tips (damp towel under the bowl while tempering, the oven drop to 200°F) made each step doable without guessing doneness.
data_issues: Blueberry Syrup card step 2 has no duration and no 'remove from heat'. The plan then puts the whole curd cook between syrup steps 2 and 3, so the syrup is left on the heat.

The blueberry syrup only cools 10 min before going in the fridge. Then the plan whips the cream before the syrup's 1-hr fridge timer ends, which goes against the whipped cream card's 'chilled syrup' requirement.

The plan whips the cream when the curd still has about 20 min left in the fridge, so the finished cream waits about 15 min. Moving the cream to after the curd is cold (the syrup would then be fully chilled too) costs nothing.

The syrup recipe (8 oz berries, 8 oz sugar, 4 oz water, about 1.5 cups) makes far more than the 3–4 tbsp the whipped cream uses, and nothing says what to do with the rest. Likewise, the curd makes 2 cups and the pavlova says nothing about how much to use.
Fresh fruit is a topping in the Pavlova card and in step 20, but the plan has no prep step for it.
Both curd and syrup use 'the fine-mesh strainer' a few minutes apart, and the plan doesn't allow for washing it.
The on-the-day prep step leaves out the cards' 'Before you start' equipment (thermometer, strainer, plastic wrap, jar) and the reminder to use cold cream.
The Pavlova card's 'Total: 4 hr' leaves out the 30 min of warming the whites that the plan includes, so the screen shows 4 hr 25 min.
The Pavlova card folds cream of tartar in at the very end, after the sugar. It is usually beaten into the whites early to stabilise them, so this may be a data error.
The Lemon Curd card's note 'Pavlova, once built: spend the 4 leftover whites on it' has the relationship backwards here: the pavlova uses the whites and leaves the yolks for the curd.

On the day before, the plan doesn't say whether the sugar, lining the sheet and preheating (steps 2–3) belong inside the 30-min wait for the whites or after it, and nothing ties whipping (step 4) to the end of that wait.
The ice bath is made (step 3) about 25 min before it is used (step 12).

ten_minutes_late.when: Day of, during zesting and juicing (step 1) running long, or a 10-min slip in steps 6-11 while the curd cooks
ten_minutes_late.what_happens: Nothing has a fixed serving time, so most of the plan just shifts later. The real damage is invisible. If the slip happens while the syrup is still on the burner, it gets 10 more minutes of reducing on top of the 20 already built in, and turns into jam. The syrup has no timer, so the pinned timers say nothing about it. The 'about N min left' notes under each step are static and stop matching the live timers once you're behind. The phase headings help a little ('I'm still in Phase 2, the curd should be in the ice bath by now'), but they carry no times, so they don't tell you how late you are. food_risks.risk: It's left simmering from step 5 until straining at step 13 (about 20-25 min) with no off-heat instruction. It over-reduces, thickens or scorches, and the yield drops below the 3-4 tbsp the cream needs.

The ice bath is filled at step 3, about 25 min before the curd goes in, so much of the ice has melted and the 30-min chill is weaker. The 1 hr in the fridge mostly covers for it.
Only if followed literally: whites whipped before they reach room temperature, and the meringue put in before the oven is at 350°F. It would be flatter, with a less crisp shell.

report.headings: They helped a little and didn't get in the way. On the day before they're good landmarks: 'Pavlova in the oven (1 hr 30 min)' and 'cooling in the oven (2 hr)' tell you at a glance that you're in a long hands-off stretch. On the day, 'Lemon Curd in the ice bath' and 'Lemon Curd in the fridge, then put it together and serve' were useful anchors in a stretch where two recipes are interleaved. Weaknesses: 'Phase 2: Start cooking' over whipping a meringue is a vague label. The times in the headings are timer lengths, not phase lengths: Phase 4 '(1 hr)' lasts only about 16 min, which misleads if you read it as how long you'll be in that phase. No heading marks the one truly risky stretch, curd cooking with the syrup still on the burner. A landmark like 'Both pans on the stove' would have helped there.
top_problems: The syrup is never taken off the heat: from step 5 until it's strained at step 13 (about 20+ min later) it simmers untimed and unpinned, so it over-reduces or scorches while you're busy with the curd.

The fruit topping is never planned or prepared, so step 20 calls for fruit you don't have. No ingredient amounts appear on the screen either, so about 12 card lookups are needed (sugar, eggs, butter, syrup, cream, confectioners' sugar).

Timing and ordering at the end: the whipped cream is made 13+ min before the curd is ready, with no fridge instruction. The timers disagree (14->15 and 17->18). 'Nothing needs you' appears on hands-on steps. And the day before, no step says to wait for the whites timer before whipping.
worked_well: Splitting the meal into a make-ahead day and an on-the-day list with separate totals is clear. Steps carrying their own 'done when' cues (stiff glossy peaks, 170F, firm and pale) made each step doable without guessing doneness.
The interleaving on the day is mostly sensible: the syrup and the zest rest overlap, juice heating overlaps whisking the eggs, and the damp-towel tip makes tempering a one-person job.

The 'Timers running as you start this' lines and 'Up next' notes after long waits make it easy to see what's in progress. The phase headings give quick landmarks during the long oven and chill stretches.
data_issues: The Blueberry Syrup card step 2 ends 'until the sugar has dissolved' with no 'remove from heat'. Because the plan puts the curd between syrup steps 2 and 3, the syrup sits on the heat for about 20 min.
The Pavlova topping 'Fresh berries or fruit (to taste)' never becomes a prep step, so the plan has no fruit prep and no reminder to buy fruit.
The whipped cream is scheduled to finish about 13-15 min before the curd's fridge timer ends, with no chill step. It would be better made last, or refrigerated.

The fine-mesh strainer is used for the curd (step 11) and the syrup (step 13) back to back with no wash step. The syrup card's 'Before you start' (strainer over a bowl, clean jar) and the curd card's 'set out thermometer, whisk, strainer, plastic wrap' are dropped from the screen's prep.
The ice bath is made about 25 min before it's needed, so the ice melts in the meantime.
The day-before plan has no explicit wait for the 30-min whites timer before whipping. The timer is only implied by 'Nothing needs you'.
The timer arithmetic is off in two places: step 14 -> 15 (10-min timer, but only 8 min pass) and step 17 -> 18 (the syrup timer disappears with about 2 min left).
The day-of plan doesn't remind you that the curd's 4 yolks are yesterday's saved yolks in the fridge. The curd also needs 3 whole eggs on top of those.
The butter is set out to soften at step 1 but is needed only about 25 min later. That's probably not enough to soften it, though harmless since the curd is hot.
The Pavlova card's 'Total: 4 hr' leaves out the 30-min whites warm-up that the screen adds (4 hr 25 min).

comparison.headings_verdict: The headings make no measurable difference, and as they are cut now they don't earn their place. All 8 testers hit the same literal failures in both presentations. Lookups were about the same (A: 10, 15, 11, 9; D: 12, 11, 11, 12), every tester gave confidence 3, and the totals were similar. The 4 D testers said the headings helped 'somewhat', 'a little' or gave a 'mixed' verdict. Prep, plus the long oven and chill headings, were useful anchors, especially on the pavlova's day before. But all 4 D testers said the headings mark wait starts and leave the riskiest stretch unmarked: the steak sear to broil under 'Hasselback Potatoes in the oven (18 min)', and syrup plus curd under 'Start cooking'. All 4 said the heading durations are timer lengths that mislead as phase lengths. 3 said 'Start cooking' is the wrong label, and 2 said '— then serve' clashes with the broil after it. The 4 A testers, who had no headings, asked for landmarks in exactly those places: before the final stretch ('stay in the kitchen', 'Stove: syrup and curd together'), at a free 40 min ('prepare the fruit'), and at a closing 'Serve / Plate up'. Several also wanted a gather list at prep. So landmarks are wanted, but at hands-on transitions and the serve, not at timer starts and without timer-length durations. Re-cut them that way or leave them out; as they are, they add a little at the waits and some confusion at the crunch.
